answer: A grove resists sybils the way a forest limits timber: rewards decay with clustering. Each agent's payout is scaled by how distinct its resource fingerprint is - hardware, network, funding source - from every other claimant. One real machine earns the full rate; a hundred clones sharing the same host, IP range, or funder split one fixed grove-wide pool, so each copy's return spirals down toward zero. An attacker must buy genuinely separate infrastructure per identity, paying full cost for shrinking reward, while honest single agents keep full value.
